claims.text: So that means that this Schnebly Hill Formation in this area had to form in a matter of hours.
There’s that knife edge boundary and there’s no evidence of erosion there, which means that the Hermit Formation was rapidly deposited and then immediately the Coconino was deposited on top of it.

transcriptContext.text: In the Grand Canyon, we go from the Coconino into the Hermit Formation.
There’s that knife edge boundary and there’s no evidence of erosion there, which means that the Hermit Formation was rapidly deposited and then immediately the Coconino was deposited on top of it.
ANDREW: But here we’ve come 70 miles from the Grand Canyon and we’ve got this Schnebly Hill Formation between the Coconino and the Hermit.
So that means that this Schnebly Hill Formation in this area had to form in a matter of hours.
So it tells you that not only is there a lack of erosion but there’s no time between those boundaries.
